transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (ZephyrSearch - Head of Product), Sana Ahmed (ZephyrSearch - Eng Manager), Omar Reyes (ZephyrSearch - ML Eng)
Shared: Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/embeddings-rerank.pdf , Security packet: https://redwood.ai/security/2027-soc2.pdf

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account, and Priya is our solutions engineer, she's gonna walk through the embeddings + rerank hosted API flow. Mark, Sana, Omar, thanks for taking time. Quick go-round on roles?
[00:12] Mark Liu: Yeah hi I'm Mark, product, trying to improve our search relevance across multi-tenant docs.
[00:16] Sana Ahmed: Sana, engineering manager, will own integration.
[00:18] Omar Reyes: Omar, ML eng, I'll be running the evaluation and pilot.
[00:22] Priya Patel: Great, quick agenda: 1) high-level product and hosted API, 2) embeddings + similarity search pattern, 3) reranking endpoint and sample pipeline, 4) Q&A and next steps. We'll keep it practical - demo with our console and curl examples.
[00:35] Alex Chen: Two quick calibration questions - what's your current infra for search? are you using Elastic + custom ranker?
[00:40] Mark Liu: We're currently on Elastic Cloud for indexing and a light BM25 baseline, with a small neural rerank in Python. Latency on rerank is around 120-200 ms per query depending on load, cost is creeping up with our CPU tier. We're hoping to drop tail latency and improve relevance for long-tail queries.
[01:00] Sana Ahmed: Also data residency is a concern, some customers require EU-only storage.
[01:05] Priya Patel: Noted. Redwood hosted API supports region selector and we can discuss EU hosted endpoints for the pilot. For private deployments we have Redwood Private but that's a larger lift - we can cover options.
[01:18] Alex Chen: Ok Priya, take it away.

--- Product & Hosted API overview ---
[01:23] Priya Patel: Our hosted API has endpoints for embeddings, search, and an explicit rerank endpoint. Typical flow: embed corpus -> index in vector DB (you can use Pinecone/FAISS or Redwood's managed vector store) -> on query, compute embedding -> candidate retrieval -> pass candidates + query to rerank endpoint which returns scored reordered results. Today I'll demo using our embeddings endpoint and the reranker. The rerank model is a lightweight cross-encoder optimized for latency and effective at short candidate lists.
[01:52] Mark Liu: Is the rerank model separate from the generation models? like different size options?
[01:56] Priya Patel: Yup, we expose multiple model families. Hosted rerank is tuned for inference speed; we also provide higher-quality models if you want deeper semantic re-ranking but with higher cost/latency. You can pin model versions, and Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization or batching tradeoffs.

--- Live demo: embeddings + rerank (console + curl) ---
[02:15] Priya Patel: Sharing screen - console -> API -> embeddings. Example curl: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" \
 -d '{"model":"rw-embed-1","input":"How do I reset my password?"}'

[02:40] Omar Reyes: Are embeddings returned as 768-d vectors by default?
[02:44] Priya Patel: It depends on model. Our rw-embed-1 returns 512 dims; we have 768 and 1024 variants. Slight mismatch sometimes in docs - the console shows model dims on the right.
[02:55] Alex Chen: Quick note - console also shows estimated token costs and typical latency per call.
[03:02] Priya Patel: Next step: index. Many teams push embeddings to Pinecone or use our managed store. We demo a small candidate set run locally: retrieve top 100, then pass to rerank. Rerank curl sample: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" \
 -d '{"model":"rw-rerank-1","query":"How do I reset my password?","candidates":[{"id":"doc1","text":"To reset password..."}, {"id":"doc2","text":"Password change steps..."}] }'

[03:42] Priya Patel: Response returns scores and a preferred ordering. We also return per-candidate explanation tokens sometimes (best-effort), and debug traces if you enable verbose tracing in the console.
[03:55] Sana Ahmed: What's the latency profile? we care about p95 < 250ms end-to-end.
[04:00] Priya Patel: For rerank of 10-50 candidates we typically see 40-120ms depending on model. End-to-end depends on retrieval; if retrieval is near-instant, rerank adds ~50-120ms. We have explicit SLOs on Dedicated with lower variance but hosted is usually pretty stable; we'll share benchmarks.
[04:18] Mark Liu: How about cost? we need to compare to our current CPU reranker costs.
[04:22] Alex Chen: We price hosted embeddings per-embedding and rerank per-request (per token or per candidate depending on model). For pilot we'll propose a capped pilot price so you can measure ROI.

--- Discussion: integration patterns & tradeoffs ---
[04:36] Priya Patel: Integration pattern A: push embeddings to vector DB + on-query embed -> kNN -> rerank. Pattern B: hybrid - use cheap BM25 to narrow, then embeddings+rerank for final ranking to reduce vector compute.
[04:55] Omar Reyes: We currently do BM25 -> small neural rerank. Sounds similar. For long documents we chunk into 512 token windows; how do you recommend chunking?
[05:05] Priya Patel: Chunk size depends on retrieval quality. Many customers use semantic chunks around 200-500 tokens and then aggregate candidate scores. Redwood Optimize can run a quick simulation and suggest chunk size/embedding model pairings.
[05:20] Mark Liu: Data security question: do you persist queries/content in hosted? we cannot log customer PII.
[05:26] Alex Chen: By default hosted keeps logs for X days for debugging. We offer controls: opt-out of retention for specific keys, customer-managed KMS for encryption, and SOC2 docs. We can also set per-customer retention policy and redact fields at ingestion. We'll send the security packet link.
[05:45] Sana Ahmed: SSO and RBAC?
[05:48] Priya Patel: Console supports SSO, SAML, and RBAC roles. For API keys you can scope keys by project and set quotas.

--- Technical deep-dive Q&A ---
[06:05] Omar Reyes: On candidate size - we plan to return top 200 from vector DB then rerank top 50. Will cost scale linearly?
[06:14] Priya Patel: Rerank cost scales with candidates, yes. We typically rerank 10-50 for latency tradeoffs. For 200 candidates you might use a cheaper filter or 2-stage rerank: coarse model first, then a cross-encoder on top 10. Redwood Optimize suggests staging.
[06:30] Mark Liu: Do you support on-the-fly batching? i.e. aggregate queries across users to amortize cost?
[06:36] Priya Patel: We have automatic batching within the runtime for compatible request shapes; it helps throughput but adds a small wait window. For low latency interactive search you can disable autos-batch. Dedicated clusters allow more aggressive batching.
[06:50] Alex Chen: Also note KV cache and attention optimizations in our runtime - for chat-style workloads they help, for rerank it's mainly cross-encoder compute.

--- Transcript realism: small transcription glitches ---
[07:05] Speaker 2: "...we saw a 20% lift when we used the new models but there waz some tail issues" (waz -> was)
[07:12] Alex Chen: (laughs) yeah we've seen tail variance on big models, that's why we recommend pinned versions for production.

--- Benchmarks & Pilot plan ---
[07:25] Priya Patel: For pilot we propose a 2-week benchmark window. You send sample logs (anonymized) and we'll run a controlled run vs your baseline. Typical metrics: relevance (NDCG), p95 latency, cost per 1k queries. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet.
[07:45] Mark Liu: How much engineering time to wire this up?
[07:48] Priya Patel: With our quickstart you can be end-to-end in a few days for a small pilot. We provide a notebook, sample code and a seed SOW if you want Redwood to run the benchmark.
[07:58] Sana Ahmed: For the EU data residency can we ensure embeddings are stored in eu-west-1?
[08:03] Priya Patel: Yes, region selector. We'll include region config in the pilot SOW. If you need private deployment (on-prem or VPC), that's a separate track.

--- Objections & tradeoffs ---
[08:18] Mark Liu: Concern: vendor lock-in, we want portability across vector stores.
[08:23] Alex Chen: Totally reasonable. Our API is storage-agnostic. You can push embeddings to any vector DB; rerank is just an API call, so if you decide to move stores, retrieval changes but rerank integration stays similar.
[08:35] Omar Reyes: Are there pre-built connectors to Elastic?
[08:38] Priya Patel: We have examples for Elastic + Pinecone and a small adapter for combining BM25 with vectors. We'll share the repo link.

--- Pricing & commercial ---
[08:50] Alex Chen: High-level pricing - embeddings per 1k, rerank per request. For pilots we can do a capped price track. If you like, I'll follow up with a custom pilot SOW and estimated tiered pricing based on your 100k monthly queries estimate.
[09:05] Mark Liu: Please do. Also curious about Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta if we scale.
[09:10] Alex Chen: Dedicated gives reserved capacity and better p95 guarantees. It's a longer contract but unit cost usually drops at scale. We'll include a sample capacity vs cost table.

--- Security specifics ---
[09:25] Sana Ahmed: Do you support customer-managed KMS for hosted?
[09:29] Priya Patel: Yes, we support KMS integration and can show key rotation docs. Also SOC2 Type II report is available in the security packet.

--- Wrap-up and next steps ---
[09:40] Alex Chen: Quick recap - Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank can drop your tail latency and improve relevance with a two-stage retrieval pipeline. We'll run a 2-week pilot that includes: run benchmarks on your logs, share SOW and pricing, provide sample rerank prompt sets, and configure EU region for data residency.
[09:57] Mark Liu: That sounds good. Omar will pull logs and sample queries.
[10:00] Omar Reyes: I'll anonymize and upload by next week.
[10:03] Alex Chen: Great - action items: Alex will send pricing and SOW, Priya will send quickstart notebook and rerank examples, Omar will supply logs. We'll target kickoff 2027-10-06.
[10:15] Sana Ahmed: One more question - what monitoring will we get during pilot?
[10:19] Priya Patel: Console provides token-level cost, p50/p95 latency, per-route dashboards, and a debug trace option. We'll share a demo dashboard screenshot.
[10:30] Mark Liu: Thanks team - appreciate the clarity.
[10:33] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and SOW; I'll include links to the sample notebook and security packet.
[10:40] Priya Patel: Bye!

Meeting notes end.
